Subject: Data eviction/playbook — questions for SLA/order form

Rishi —

Thanks for taking this on. We need to lock down the retention and deletion language for the order form so procurement can complete the review. A few pragmatic questions to help us draft the schedules: 

- Can Redwood support multiple retention tiers per account (e.g., Transient = 30 days, Standard = 90 days, Archive = 365 days) and map them per dataset or per model route?
- For deletion requests, what is the operational timeline from request to irrevocable deletion? Specifically we need a guaranteed maximum time and a description of the deletion process (snapshot removal, overwrite/crypto-key destruction, backups).
- Do you provide a formal deletion certificate or attestations (for audit/soc2 evidence)? If so, what does that include and how quickly can we get it after deletion completes?
- For e-discovery or regulatory holds, can you suspend deletion for named datasets/keys and for how long? Any cost/impact we should expect?
- Residency: we need a playbook for customers with mixed residency (US primary + EU backup). How are deletions coordinated across regions to ensure consistent timelines and proofs?

Also attaching a template of the clause our legal team prefers to see — they're open to language but want the guarantees. Can you respond with concrete SLA wording we can include and call out any exceptions (e.g., disaster recovery backups, forensic hold windows)?

Thanks — Jared
Jared Klein
Director, IT Procurement
Peregrine Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Data eviction/playbook — questions for SLA/order form

Jared —

Appreciate the detail. High level answers up front, then proposed order-form language below. I cc'd Lauren (legal) to confirm the tightenables.

Short answers: 
- Yes: we support per-route/dataset retention tiers. Customers can designate routes or data labels to a retention class on the account config and we persist that mapping as part of the order form.
- Deletion timeline: we guarantee initiation of deletion within 24 hours of an authenticated request, with irrevocable removal from active serving and KV caches within 72 hours. Backups and long-term snapshots are purged on a 30-day schedule (i.e. fully irrecoverable after 30 days from the deletion initiation).
- Deletion evidence: we provide a Deletion Attestation (PDF) that includes timestamps for request/initiation/completion, IDs of artifacts removed, and hashes of destroyed snapshots where applicable. Attestation delivered within 5 business days.
- Legal holds: we can apply a preserve flag to any named dataset; preserved data is excluded from automated eviction and incurs a small monthly stewarding fee. Holds can be time-limited or indefinite (billing continues until release).
- Multi-region coordination: deletions are coordinated via the control plane. For mixed-residency accounts we execute deletion in the primary region first and then trigger region-specific purge jobs; the attestation will list per-region completion times. Cross-region propagation is included in the 72-hour window for active data and the 30-day snapshot purge for backups.

Proposed order-form excerpts (suggested, can be redlined):

1) Retention classes: Customer may assign datasets or model routes to one of the following classes: Transient (30 days), Standard (90 days), Extended (365 days). Assignments are recorded in the Order Form Appendix A and may be updated by mutual written agreement.

2) Deletion initiation and completion: Upon receipt of an authenticated deletion request from Customer, Redwood will initiate deletion within 24 hours. Active-serving data (including live indexes, KV caches, and immediate caches) will be removed within 72 hours. Remaining backups, snapshots, and disaster-recovery copies will be purged according to the snapshot purge schedule; Redwood warrants that such artifacts will be rendered irrecoverable no later than 30 days from deletion initiation.

3) Attestation: Redwood will provide a Deletion Attestation within 5 business days of completion certifying the artifacts removed, the timestamps for each region, and cryptographic hashes of removed snapshot manifests where applicable.

4) Legal hold / preservation: Customer may place a Preservation Hold on specified datasets; Redwood will suspend automated deletion for those datasets and retain them until release. Preservation Holds may be subject to an administrative fee and will be reflected in billing while in effect. Redwood will provide a notice to Customer within 48 hours when a Preservation Hold affects automated eviction schedules.

5) Exceptions: Emergency snapshots retained for forensic or disaster recovery purposes may be subject to extended retention; Redwood will notify Customer and provide a justification and timeline. Any exceptions will be limited to documented incident response events.

Attachments: I attached a clean draft with the above language and a short appendix describing the evidence format (Peregrine_SLA_Eviction_Playbook_Draft_v2.pdf). Also including a small zip with sample attestations and a sample purge manifest schema (Redwood_Evidence_Samples.zip).

If that matches your needs I can ask Lauren to do the formal redlines and then circulate a DocuSign. FYI: the preservation hold billing and attestation delivery timelines are non-negotiable from an operational standpoint (those are tied to our purge cadence and audit batch jobs).

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

- Retention classes: Transient (30d), Standard (90d), Extended (365d) as described in Appendix A of the attached Order Form.

- Exceptions: Forensic/DR snapshots require documented approval and have a limited extension window per incident.
